tasks.gr9-imagery-and-symbolism-in-poems-t2: Topic: Imagery and symbolism in poems. Cover imagery that appeals to the senses (sight, sound, touch, smell, taste), symbols, extended metaphor, and how images and symbols carry the poem's meaning and mood. Use only original poems or public-domain poems that are cited. Ask Grade 9 learners to quote an image, name the sense it appeals to, and explain what it suggests.
tasks.gr9-form-and-structure-in-poems-t2: Topic: Form and structure in poems. Cover stanza forms (couplet, tercet, quatrain), rhymed verse and free verse, enjambment and end-stopped lines, caesura, the sonnet (fourteen lines, quatrains and a couplet, a turn in thought) and how form supports meaning. Use only original poems or public-domain poems that are cited. Ask Grade 9 learners to describe the form of a poem and explain why it suits the content.
tasks.gr9-tone-mood-irony-and-message-t3: Topic: Tone, mood, irony and the poet's message. Cover tone (the attitude of the speaker, with a range of tone words), mood (the atmosphere and the feeling it gives the reader), verbal and situational irony, contrast, and how to state and support the poet's message. Use only original poems or public-domain poems that are cited. Ask Grade 9 learners to identify tone and mood from the words and to explain the irony and the message with quotations.
tasks.gr9-analysing-a-poem-and-writing-poetry-: Topic: Analysing a poem, answering contextual poetry questions and writing a poem. Cover a method for analysing a poem (title, speaker, subject, structure, language and sound, tone and mood, message), types of contextual questions (literal, figurative, word choice, tone and mood, evaluation) with model answers, and writing a poem of four to eight stanzas: planning, drafting, revising and presenting. Use only original poems. Ask Grade 9 learners to support every point with a quotation and an explanation.
